In the present study, set of process parameters to be optimized are gap voltage, current, pulse ON time and multi walled carbon nanotube powder concentration in dielectric used in Electrical Discharge Machining (EDM) process. These parameters are investigated to identify the variations the performance characteristics of material removal rate and surface roughness. The material used for machining NAK80 Steel is a copper electrode. Based on the four factors at three levels, Taguchi's L9 orthogonal array is selected for carrying out the experiments. The objective of the present study is to get higher rate of material removal and lower surface roughness. The optimal solution is obtained by using Taguchi's Grey Relational Analysis method. MINITAB software was used to find the optimal levels of parameters in EDM process. The optimum result obtained was tested by carrying out the confirmation experiment. Based on the confirmation test, the improvements in material removal rate and surface roughness were 25% and 6.87% respectively. It is found from the present study that Taguchi's Grey relational Analysis is an effective technique to optimize the process parameters for Electric Discharge Machining.

articleTitle: A novel colour image encryption algorithm based on linear canonical transform
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: A novel algorithm for the colour image encryption is proposed in this paper. Proposed algorithm is based on image scrambling and Linear canonical Transform. The image scrambling accomplished using the chaotic function with iterations along the length of the image to be scrambled. The Linear canonical transform (LCT) is used to encrypt all the three components of colour image i.e. Red, Green and Blue at the same time. Application of the LCT over these components makes to not affect each other. So the connections between Red, Green and Blue components is condensed in the encrypted components. The security of the colour image is increased using the proposed algorithm. Simulation results represents that the proposed algorithm is best suited for the colour image encryption as well it provide safety to various attacks.

articleTitle: Gripmitt: An electronic exoskeleton for improved hand movement
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Grip is the result of sequence of operations including opening of hand, positioning of fingers, bringing the fingers closer to the object and maintaining the hold of an object. Gripping is a problem in many people, may it be patients with brain injury, spinal cord injury, nerve injury, fractures and many more. The formation of the grip requires action of flexors and extensors of wrist and fingers. If any of these is affected, this grip will be affected or it may also be lost. Problems in gripping hampers even the basic activities of daily life's, like picking up a glass of water, wringing clothes, holding a bottle, etc. This increases the dependency of the patient on others and thus reduces the quality of life. Cylindrical grip is one of the most powerful grips that enable a person to grab cylindrical objects like a glass of water, a bottle, etc. Other types of grip includes spherical grip, point grip etc. Here, we introduce Gripmitt. This device provides an external assistance to the user to make a cylindrical grip possible. In order to achieve this, the patient's functioning of the shoulder and elbow needs to be intact. This device operates on verbal commands given by the patient himself. Voice of the patient and function of each verbal command is pre-stored in the module. Patient needs no external assistance once the device is fitted on his/her hand. The device can be easily mounted and unmounted from the patient's hand and it can be effectively used.

articleTitle: Impact of vehicle emission and development by OEM
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: In this era of automobile, in manufacturing point of view, every Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) has to consider various parameters while manufacturing a vehicle. Emission is one of the important parameter. As emission is harmful to the surrounding, Indian government has set some emission norms to control it. OEM has to manufacture a vehicle by keeping these emission norms into consideration. But now, Indian Government is changing its emission norms in April 2020 and will make it more rigid. This sudden change in emission norms is the main challenge; OEM's has to face, for manufacturing a vehicle in such a short span of time. OEM's has proposed some technologies which will be suitable for future emission norms.

articleTitle: SecTrans: Enhacing user privacy on Android Platform
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Interchange of information through cell phones, Tabs and PDAs (Personal Digital Assistant) is the new trend in the era of digitization. In day-to-day activities, sensitive information through mobile phones is exchanged among the users. This sensitive information can be in the form of text messages, images, location, etc. The research on Android mobile applications was done at the MIT, and found that applications are leaking enormous amount of information to the third party servers. 73 percent of 55 Android applications were detected to leak personal information of the users [8]. Transmission of files securely on Android is a big issue. Therefore it is important to shield the privacy of user data on Android operating system. The main motive of this paper is to protect the privacy of data on Android Platform by allowing transmission of textual data, location, pictures in encrypted format. By doing so, we achieved intimacy and integrity of data.

articleTitle: Vendor evaluation and ranking system using TOPSIS for air conditioners manufacturer
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This paper relates to the case study of evaluation of vendors considering both quantitative as well as qualitative factors. This case study involves ranking and evaluation of air conditioner manufacturing firm. The paper uses MADM technique TOPSIS (Technique for Order of Prioritization by Similarity to Ideal Solution) for this evaluation. The system allowed on multi-attributes criteria like Cost of AHU, Quality in temperature sensitivity, Service for timely-delivery and Reliability for warrantee/guarantee period. In order to compute and examine their performance, vendor evaluation is used. This helps to reduce costs and risks associated with it thereby propelling continuous evaluation.

articleTitle: Fabrication of tapered and conductive microcantilever
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) are unified micro devices or systems combining both electrical and mechanical components. Microcantilevers are the most simplified device of MEMS. Moreover, in the last few years the technology has been developed for the fabrication of microcantilever as a sensing device. The sensitivity of the microcantilever depends upon its geometry as well as the material. Varying profile has better sensitivity than the uniform profile. Also, material with less modulus of elasticity gives more deflection. Most of the polymer possess less modulus of elasticity than silicone and hence better suited for fabricating microcantilever as a sensor. However due to lack of conductivity, conductive fillers need to be added in order to fabricate conductive microcantilever. This paper describes an economical and simpler method of fabricating varying width and depth profile as well as conducting microcantilever using sequential micro-milling as well as micro-moulding process. In this method the replica of micro-cantilever beam is made on a Brass substrate using micro milling method and then micro-cantilever is produced by using polymer nanocomposite as moulding material followed by micro-moulding process. Polymer poldimethylsiloxane (PDMS) and conductive filler Carbon Black (CB) is used to prepare polymer nanocomposite in this work.

articleTitle: Impact of faults on the efficiency of squirrel cage induction motor
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Faults in any power system are the outcome of an undesirable and unexpected set of conditions that have taken place in the system. They have a major impact on all the dependent equipments or machines and adversely affect their performance. The effect of fault on the efficiency helps in the early detection of the fault, even before the severeness of the fault has reached the level that enables relays to act. This paper analyses the impact of faults like voltage unbalance, broken rotor bar and air gap eccentricity, on efficiency of a three phase squirrel cage induction motor. These faults are simulated in MATLAB Simulink by mathematical modelling of Induction Motor and drop in efficiency is estimated.

articleTitle: Material optimization and experimental analysis of shock & vibration mount
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Shock and vibration (SV) mounting system improves durability of engine and other running machine by reducing unwanted motion. This system is used extensively to isolate machinery (industrial & marine), civil engineering structure (base isolation in building, bridges etc.) and sensitive components from foundation/base. In addition to the above, in vehicular, marine & some industrial machine as well as seismic application, isolators are also expect to lower the impact of shock from base to isolators object and vice-versa. As rubber is soft and visco-elastic material it has a unique combination of elastic (spring) and viscous (damping) properties makes it very useful material for SV mount. Generally SV mount consist of vulcanized rubber bonded to metal part which facilitate load distribution and installation. For this development work, Hydrogenated Nitrile Butadiene Rubber (HNBR) elastomer is used as shock and vibration absorbing part of mount as this elastomer can be designed to get better mechanical properties with improved service life.

articleTitle: Electromagnetic energy harnessing using rectenna approach
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: In this paper the idea of harnessing energy from radio waves is explained. An RF energy harvesting system is shown which receives energy from frequencies 900MHz-2.45GHz. The main element of the system is a rectenna, which is an integration of antenna array and a rectifier circuit. The RF signals are collected using an array of microstrip antennas and dipole antennas. The design and simulation of these antennas are presented. The rectangular microstrip antenna is resonant at 2.45GHz with a simulation bandwidth of 30MHz. The return loss of a 4 × 4 microstrip antenna is as low as -18dB. And the dipole antenna which is resonant at 900MHz has the simulation bandwidth of 100MHz at the return loss of 17.2 dB. An FR-4 substrate with a dielectric constant of 4.4 and a loss tangent of 0.02 is used for simulation in IE3D and HFSS.

articleTitle: Evaluating performance of RF MEMS switch at elevated temperatures
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The numerical modeling of a microelectromechanical System (MEMS) switch consisting of a suspended gold membrane on a coplanar waveguide (CPW) is presented. In this work, the effect of length, width, and thickness of micro-cantilever beam on deflection, natural frequency and quality factor at different operational temperatures are numerically modeled. Further fabrication process flow is presented. Our results show that, the modeling of device performance based on the effects of device geometry parameters would help in providing valuable insight for the micro-fabrication process.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation and optimization of Oxy-Acetylene assisted machining parameters for Nickel based alloy Inconel — 718
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This paper presents an experimental investigation of Inconel-718 nickel based alloy using Oxy-Acetylene Assisted Machining (OAAM) process, which is difficult-to-cut at room temperature and then results in disproportionate tool wear and poor surface finish. The workpiece surface is heated just before machining operation starts. This is done using external heat source till the set value of temperature is attained, due to heating the material surface is soften which enhances the material removal rate. The set value of temperature is constant while turning the workpiece surface using temperature control system on conventional lathe machine with the help of tungsten carbide cutting tool. This paper presents the design of experiment based on Taguchi method which is used to find the optimal cutting parameters for surface roughness. In this study, the methodology of L9 orthogonal array, signal-to-noise (S/N) ratio and analysis of variance (ANOVA) is applied to synthesize the effect of these parameters on Nickel based alloy Inconel-718.

articleTitle: Process parameter optimization for computer numerical control turning on En36 alloy steel
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: In this investigation we have considered EN36 alloy steel matterial for optimization of process parameters. Turning En36 takes more time to machine with maintaining good quality of surface roughness. So material removal rate (MRR) and surface roughness (SR) is considered as response parameter and input parameters are speed, feed, depth of cut (DOC). Taguchi and ANOVA tool is used for optimization.

articleTitle: Experimental investigation on taper angle of micro-electro discharge machining based on Taguchi Method
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The need of non-traditional producing has been making small options and irregular contours like within the producing of holes and surfaces with sharp corners and contours for die and moulds creating. within the recent years one in every of the foremost vital technologies in non-ancient producing is micro-EDM (Electric discharge machining). micro-EDM may be a method for getting burr free small options with high aspect ratio wherever machining is finished by fast electrical spark discharges between the piece of work and gear leading to melting and vaporizing of tool and piece of work. Since EDM may be a non-contact machining method. Its applications starting from reaction-propulsion engine parts to hot extrusion moulds wherever toughness and sturdiness square measure needed at high temperatures. The influence of 4 parameters specifically Discharge current (A), Pulse on Time (B), Feed Rate (C), spindle speed (D) on Tapper Angle (TA) are studied and therefore the experiments are conducted based on Taguchi technique with L9 orthogonal array with four columns and nine rows to desire the optimized taper angle of nickel based super alloy 718 specimen for Micro-EDM.

articleTitle: Agility through design automation: A study on centrifugal pump design
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to study the basic concepts of agile manufacturing, its enablers and applications in industry. The paper also concentrates on how this concept of agile manufacturing can be used effectively in centrifugal pump industry for design process. With the presented work the author has tried to automate the design of centrifugal pump using macros in CATIA V5. The pump manufacturing industry will able to meet the dynamic requirements of customer in very short duration of time. In this work, author tried to take the input parameters in MS Excel and using parametric relations all other dimensions are calculated. These values are read using macros in CATIA and the part drawings along with their assembly drawing are generated. The user will also be able to extract 2D views from part drawings and assembly drawing. All the part drawings and 2D drawings will be saved automatically at specified folder. The time required for repetitive task is reduced considerably. In this way the customer demands can be responded quickly and agility can be achieved.

articleTitle: Laboratory experiments for understanding effects of RF impairments on received signal in satellite link
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Satellite communication becomes a complacent subject for undergraduate students as not many high end equipment or accurate, clear and well interpreted simulated results are available. Given this limitation in the availability of resources, conducting a laboratory becomes a challenging task. Hence, this paper has been carried out as an extension of Radiofrequency satellite Link on Matlab r2016b. The electromagnetic signal carrying information is inflicted upon a lot of impairments such as Free Space Path Loss, Memoryless Nonlinearity, etc. In the current Simulink radio frequency (RF) satellite Link model, these impairments are modeled in the form of respective blocks with the provision of various mask parameters in each of them which allows us to vary those parameters to see the corresponding changes in the nature of the signal. The primary objective of this paper is to carry out experiments on the similar lines as aforementioned dealing with all impairments and corresponding results are discussed followed by a conclusion. Increasing free space path loss led all the signal points coming closer to each other in their constellation diagram. Memoryless nonlinearity due to High Power Amplifier (HPA) tends to greatly displace all the points in a circular fashion from grid/square form. Thermal noise at the receiver has its effects on the outer constellation points. Phase noise spreads the signal points across their usual location. In-phase/Quadrature phase (I/Q) of the 16-QAM modulated signal's amplitude and phase change led to dynamic motion of signal points oscillating towards In-phase amplitude and Quadrature-phase amplitude axes.

articleTitle: SpO2 based supplemental oxygen delivery system for soldiers at extreme altitudes
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This paper presents an automatic system to deliver supplemental oxygen to soldiers patrolling at extreme altitudes based on their SpO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> (blood oxygen saturation) levels. The paper emphasizes on electronic hardware designed for functioning at extreme altitudes featuring low barometric pressures, low temperatures and humidity. The software safety checks incorporated into the system are critical in ensuring the functional reliability of the system in field conditions. The system reads SpO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sub> levels of the subject from a wrist-worn pulse oximeter module through wireless interface and controls a proportional solenoid valve to regulate the oxygen supply to the subject. The oxygen is delivered from a lightweight portable oxygen cylinder through nasal nares.

articleTitle: ZAIMUS: A department automation system using data mining and web technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This paper gives details about web-based department automation system which will be implemented at educational institution level for maintaining faculty details and records. The proposed application aims at providing efficient and hassle-free working environment for faculty of the organization as it reduces the amount of paperwork involved. This system is based on the modern approach of data mining and web technology which overcomes the drawbacks of existing manual method used by the educational institution reducing mistakes and errors in record keeping. The system provides faster computation of queries to fetch data from a huge database. The application is designed using Eclipse (kepler version), Apache Tomcat server 7.0 along with wamp server to host the database locally. J2EE, JSP along with Html have been used for designing the user interface whereas MySQL database is used for storing data.

articleTitle: An overview on renovation and modernization of existing substations
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This paper provides information regarding electrical equipment which are currently used in substations with new techniques for operation, maintenance, monitoring, control and improved performance by implementing modern equipments. An overview on combined features of all upgraded technology, related to achieve optimum results, space management and its effects on system are discussed. The purpose is to fulfill demands of the modern substation. To achieve this, various technical, economic and environmental factors, such as cost, safety, security, controllability, flexibility and reliability are to be considered. These factors require the use of modern techniques and equipments different from existing one. The objective is focused on cost reduction in long term usage while maintaining the performance of entire system.

articleTitle: Analysis of failed and working power transformer and their diagnostics
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The Transformer sustains various types of faults while in the working condition. There will be changes in electrical, mechanical and chemical properties in different parts of transformer before its failure. These changes in properties can be monitored by different condition monitoring methods. With proper analyzing the results of conditioning monitoring test the transformer can be easily saved from complete failure. In this paper various condition monitoring methodologies and its results analysis are explained by discussing the different case studies of failed and saved transformers.

articleTitle: Performance simulation of optimized stock 2014 Ducati Panigale 899 for quarter mile drag racing
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The primary objective of this research is to convert a stock motorcycle into a drag strip motorcycle and optimize it for best performance in terms of elapsed time in a quarter mile (1320 feet) drag strip. Stock 2014 Ducati Panigale 899 has been used as a reference motor cycle model. The motorcycle is modeled using several models such as engine model, drivetrain model, tire model, chassis model, throttle control model, and track model to simulate the operation, and to try and bring it close to real-time performance as possible. MATLAB software package is used for optimizing and simulating the motorcycle. First, stock motor cycle models are developed and simulated using the software package, to see the performance and elapsed time in a quarter mile drag strip. Further, optimized models are developed by varying the vehicle parameters to models to simulate and validate the real time performance. This paper gives an approach for optimizing a drag racer motor cycle model. Research is focused on improving the laps timing for quarter mile drag racing, and successfully achieved with the approach taken. A global application algorithm is generated for this research can also be used for the other motor cycle models for simulation, optimization, and validation for a quarter mile run.

articleTitle: Finite element analysis of Femur prosthesis
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This study is based on advancement in Bio-Medical engineering. Computer Aided Design (CAD) and Finite Element Analysis (FEA) in prosthesis design for bone is a critical application of mechanical engineering. Different materials with varying mechanical properties are used; deformations and stresses for different loading conditions are calculated and finally optimized to have maximum effective life of an implant. CAD and the FEA have revolutionized way, the prosthesis are designed and developed. This work is carried out in four stages; compression testing of bone using Universal Testing Machine (UTM), 3D Scanning of Natural Femur Bone is done using white light scanning camera, prosthesis modeling using Pro-E, static and dynamic analysis of the prosthesis is done using ANSYS tool.

articleTitle: Economics of distribution feeder conditioning: Modelling and analysis-A case study
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This work investigates the voltage profiles of multiple distribution feeders and unbalanced problems of interconnected feeders. To maintain the required voltage levels as per ANSI standards different conventional techniques like On-load tap changing, switched Capacitor Banks, Voltage regulators and wire works are adopted. This paper also presents some of the basics and advanced methods of feeder conditioning. The power system has been modeled and analyzed for the imbalance of voltages to arrive at the optimum economical solution. A community in Belvidere, North Carolina has been considered for the case study. This work is estimated to be a useful benchmark for personnel in electrical utilities to arrive at the optimum economical solutions within the existing system. It also, gives a gist of the practical solutions possible for conditioning of the distribution feeders to the academicians.

articleTitle: Influence of non uniform heating and porous medium on performance of micro channel heat sink
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The increase in requirement for heat dissipation in thermal management application has led to the development of new techniques. Heat sink with micro pin fin is one of the effective techniques which have attracted the researcher in past two decades. In the present work the performance of un finned Micro channel heat sink (MCHS), heat sink with circular pin fin (CPF) and heat sink with square pin fin (SPF) are numerically analyzed to access the hydrodynamic and heat transfer behavior for Reynolds number ranging between 100 to 900 using water as coolant. Three different cases of heat flux namely uniform, linear and sinusoidal were examined using three dimensional conjugate heat transfer model. According to the results obtained from the present work heat sink with square pin fin and uniform heat flux has higher heat transfer coefficient and pressure drop. Furthermore the influence of porous medium on the performance of heat sink were studied. Results reveal that hydrodynamic and heat transfer characteristics are greatly influenced by size and location of porous medium.

articleTitle: Image registration on biomedical images with composite algorithm
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Image registration, a technique of alignment of two different images sharing familiar information, is a crucial step in most of image processing applications that needs visual information from numerous images for evaluation or analysis. Four image processing techniques viz. geometric transformation, discrete cosine transform, phase correlation & log polar transform (LPT) for image registration are implemented. However, limitations in terms of implementation of all these operations simultaneously still exist in image registration applications. This paper provides in depth analysis of LPT, its advantages like relevant information to medical practitioner. Log-polar techniques are proposed to address above limitation so that all these operations can be carried out in sink.

articleTitle: Estimation of chlorophyll based on FPGA and Matlab
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: In today's modern era a theoretical based approach is followed to determine the amount of chlorophyll present in leaves of plants. But in this paper a practical based approach is followed to generate an architecture of simple, low cost Chlorophyll estimator using Field Programmable Gate Array(FPGA). Color of leaf can give an indication for assessing plant health and nutrient. Performance analysis of several regression model shows that multivariate regression model with nonlinear terms provides best fit between estimated terms. We found that the residuals are near in baseline and the adjusted coefficient of determination is very significant. Root mean square error (RMSE), standard deviation, variance and mean of some leaf image samples is taken. A digital system is generated in which Matlab input is used in Xilinx and synthesized results are generated using Verilog code.

articleTitle: Comparative performance study of various filters on high density impulse noise
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The paper compares the performance of various filters of different sizes on impulse noise in spatial domain. In this paper median and adaptive median filters are used from non-linear category. For a low density impulse noise, smaller size median filter is required while for a high density impulse noise, either a larger size median filter is required or a series of smaller size median filter is required. The circular averaging filter also performs well in this case but at the expense of more blurring. Moreover alpha trimmed mean filter works well with a moderate density impulse noise. Finally the adaptive median filter works best on impulse noise. The adaptive median filter can recover the image even if the image is not visible in case of very high density impulse noise. The paper demonstrates some novel procedures involving a series of filters to handle high density impulse noise.

articleTitle: A DSP based reprogrammable architecture for standalone signal processing applications
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Signal Processing applications with an end to end analog interface are primitively implemented by using a hardcoded DSP or MCU unit to execute predefined algorithms. However, when a need to reconfigure the existent system arises, it involves reprogramming the whole system once again. Also in the case of an iterative process, while fine tuning the system, such an approach is tedious in nature. Hardware emulators that can configure a user-defined signal flow are expensive and are based on an architecture that is incapable of executing the algorithm once the emulator is disconnected from the host computer. This paper describes a novel architecture of a hardware emulator that is independent of the connection state with its host since the emulator itself is responsible for executing the signal flow through its hard coded algorithm. Digital Manipulator of Analog Signals (DMAS) is a hardware unit that is constructed for verification of the algorithm for the hardware emulator and related results are subsequently presented in the paper.

articleTitle: Analysis of fuzzy with neuro-fuzzy approach to self-tune database system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The Database Management system (DBMS) and other system software are used to store and retrieve large amounts of data in a structured way. The modern applications are generally data intensive and involve frequent storage of data and rapid access to them. To drive such applications and to support highly dynamic user load, the database system needs to be tuned systematically. To tune the database system, the database administrator (DBA) has to continuously monitor the DBMS and several other system parameters so as to enhance the performance of the system, and also ensure proper utilization of system resources. The manual tuning is not only tedious, but it may also result in system instability due to over or under-tuning of system parameters. Hence, the trend in modern database systems is to implement self-tuning mechanisms to relieve the DBA of the tedious task. The control architecture proposed is based on the Fuzzy Logic and Neural Networks. The proposed method has been validated under TPC-C workload and has shown significant improvement in performance. The comparison is also made between Fuzzy tuning and Neural network-Fuzzy tuning. With a self-tuning system in place, results have improved performance, with Neuro-Fuzzy Approach.

articleTitle: Simulation study of active vibration control of beams supported at both ends using optimal controllers
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This paper deals with the design of different optimal controllers for attenuating the vibration of beams supported at both ends, viz. fixed-fixed and fixed-roller beams which form multiple input and multiple output (MIMO) system. The beam structure consists an array of sensors and actuators, mounted in a collacated manner at the root of the beam, coupled with a controller. Finite element model of the beam is obtained using ANSYS©, and through the modal analysis eigen values and eigen vectors are extracted. The state space matrices of the beam structures are obtained by mathematical modelling which is done in MATLAB©. The simulation study is performed using three optimal controllers, viz. Linear Quadratic Regulator (LQR), Linear Quadratic Gaussian (LQG), and H-<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub>, governed by state feedback and output feedback control laws. To reduce the computational time, the significantly contributing modes are considered. LQR controller gain is determined by considering the quadratic cost function. LQG regulator is obtain by combining the LQR gain and Kalman gain. H-<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">∞</sub> controllers maintains the stability and robustness of the system within prescribed limits. The simulation results of these three optimal controllers are further compared and the significant finding are reported in the paper.

articleTitle: Gain and bandwidth improvement of microstrip antenna using RIS and FPC resonator
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Improvement in gain as well as bandwidth of microstrip antenna using reactive impedance surface and Fabry Perot cavity resonator is proposed. Suspended microstrip antenna (MSA) is designed on reactive impedance surface (RIS) backed FR4 substrate. RIS improves bandwidth, gain and efficiency of antenna due to reduced coupling between MSA and ground plane. This MSA backed RIS is placed in a FPC resonator for further improving the gain of MSA. 1×1 to 4×4 square patch arrays are designed on a dielectric layer which is energized by the radiations from RIS backed MSA. The PRS layer is placed at about λ<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">0</sub>/2 from ground. The S11 is <; -9.5 dB over 5.725-6.4 GHz. Maximum gain of 15.8 dBi with gain variation <; 2 dB is obtained using 4×4 array. Beside this, cross polarization and Side lobe level are <; -2ο dB. Antenna offers front to back lobe ratio (FBR) > 20 dB and > 70 % antenna efficiency. The measured results of prototype structure are in agreement with the simulation results.

articleTitle: Advances in smart wheelchair technology
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: A Survey of Disabled Persons by NSSO (2011) reported that Disability is an important public health problem in India. The wheelchair is topmost used assistive devices for enhancing the personal mobility of disabled people. Power wheelchairs are useful for those unable to propel a manual wheelchair. The disabled people with visual acuity, lack of motor skills and strength find difficult to use a power wheelchair. To solve this problem, several researchers have used mobile robots technologies to create smart wheelchairs. A smart wheelchair typically contains a standard power wheelchair, a computer and a collection of sensors. The recent development in research areas such as computer science, robotics, Artificial Intelligence and sensor technology broaden the range of features in smart wheelchairs. This paper presents designs of different prototypes of smart wheelchairs proposed by researchers. Future research challenges in this field are recognized. Also, Directions for upcoming research are discussed.

articleTitle: Stationary electrical energy storage technology for global energy sustainability: A review
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Today our life depends on electricity. With increase in demand, requirement of electricity generation is also increasing day by day. Energy should be transferred from fossil fuel to other energy sources. Stationary electrical energy storage technology is reported to be safe, flexible, unlimited and reliable. Goal of global energy sustainability is to replace the fossil fuel by renewable energy and to reduce the emission of greenhouse gases. This paper describes the requirements and various challenges of global energy sustainability. The paper also presents the role of energy storage in electricity supply network, different electrical energy storage technologies, control and power conditioning system, comparison of high power technologies including various important high power applications in research and industry.

articleTitle: Vibration measurement on mini helicopter for electro-optic payload integration
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Autonomous mini helicopters are gaining popularity towards crowd monitoring, disaster management, intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance. This is due to its advantage of vertical take-off and landing along with electro-optic payload carrying capability. The present work is a technology demonstrator project wherein a radio controlled mini helicopter is being converted into autonomous mini helicopter with objective of intelligence, surveillance and reconnaissance. Most of these mini helicopters are fitted with a small two stroke piston engine to generate torque for rotating main rotor and tail rotor. The engine and rotor blades are the major sources of mechanical, aerodynamic and acoustic vibrations in the airframe. In the present paper vibrations are measured and analyzed at different locations on the airframe from the vibration isolation point of view. The main objectives of this work are to capture the baseline vibration profile of helicopter and to study the effectiveness of the passive vibration isolators in achieving stabilized video from the electro-optic (EO) payload integrated to mini helicopter.

articleTitle: Parametric study on Oxy hydrogen gas generation and associated energy consumption using Taguchi's design of experiment concept
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Oxy hydrogen gas is used for lighting, heating, welding etc and in recent past as a fuel additive in internal combustion engines. Generation of Oxy hydrogen gas depends upon number of factors like current, molarity, temperature etc. This paper presents parametric study on rate of oxy hydrogen gas generation (RGN) and related energy consumption (EC). Study is divided in two stages. In the first stage, experimentation is carried out using Taguchi's design of experiment concept to identify the significance of each factor on both responses. Regression model is presented to obtain RGN and EC at different levels of selected factors. Current shows its strong significance on both responses and its difficult to interpret contributions of other selected factors. In the second stage, these contributions are investigated at constant current. Optimization is carried out for maximum RGN and minimum EC with response surface methodology. Interaction effects are also studied and commented.

articleTitle: Future prospects of energy efficient smart home in India
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: The residential sector in India, accounting for 22% of total energy produced, is one of the sector where the largest uncaptured energy productivity improvement opportunity lie. Home appliance penetration will be particularly domineering in driving residential energy demand growth in India, which is urbanizing at a rapid rate. The focus in the research community is to condense energy wastage in dwellings in order to improve global energy efficiency. Since the reserves of fossil fuels are limited, the use of alternative energy sources needs to be encouraged. This paper presents a brief overview on the various architectures and functional modules of smart home energy management system (HEMS), integration of renewable resources in smart HEMS and intelligent monitoring and control of home appliances to reduce domestic energy usage, a challenging target to mitigate energy crisis and the environmental problems. Also, we discussed future prospects and challenges for energy efficient smart home system in India.

articleTitle: Identifying organizational factors affecting individual knowledge creation
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: In recent years, the importance of keeping and sharing knowledge in organization have motivated many firms to start knowledge management (KM) projects. However, in reality, many of KM projects have failed or not achieved the planned goals. Lack of infrastructure for knowledge creation are known as one of the important reasons for this failure. Knowledge creation is one of the main level in KM cycle. Knowledge and knowledge creating tools, if well recognized and applied, have a significant role in the success of the KM project. The aim of this study is to identify organizational factors that affect individual knowledge creation in the firm. The systematic literature review resulted in 23 key factors on individual knowledge creation. These factors were classified in five categories namely: organizational culture, strategy, organizational structure, human resources and information technologies. Focusing on these factors, can increase knowledge creation by employees in organization and decrease the rate of KM projects failure.

articleTitle: Structural equation modeling for performance of public distribution system
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: This research aimed to develop a structural equation model of performance of public distribution system (PDS) in Amravati District, Maharashtra State. The sample consisted of 300 customers of multi-stage sampling. Data was significantly statistical analyzed by using SPSS/AMOS statistical software. The results indicated the developed model was valid and fitted to empirical data. The factors of targeting error, delivery mechanism, information asymmetry, customer satisfaction and cost were significantly and positively related to PDS performance. Customer satisfaction factor was the highest direct effect on PDS performance while targeting error was the highest indirect effect. A clear understanding of the postulated relationships among the studied variables might encourage the FPSs to figure out appropriate course of action to improve PDS performance by reducing the targeting error and information asymmetry in order to satisfy customer and reduced the cost.

articleTitle: Design and modeling of low power alternator for solar thermal application
publicationTitle: 2017 International Conference on Nascent Technologies in Engineering (ICNTE)
abstract: Harvesting of renewable energy for power generation has become the need of the hour. Among the various types of renewable energy sources, the solar thermal application stands out. This application has several advantages and requires mainly a low power alternator and other special components for power generation. The paper presents the design of low power alternator being used in roof top solar thermal conversion system. The design parameters of stator and rotor construction, winding configuration and other crucial factors of a typical low power alternator have been discussed. The material requirement for the construction of alternator has been worked out and presented. Further, the mathematical modeling of synchronous generator has been presented.
